# Mount Vernon native scene-layer runtime

The TSMNative world subsystem `UTSMSceneLayerSubsystem` provides actual native Unreal actor visibility controls, a 14-layer semantic catalog, source-registration states and JSON visibility profile save/load. It is intentionally independent of any online service, works with Cesium or other actors already instantiated in the world, and uses the existing TSMNative module export macro.

**No city geometry or verified utility topology is generated by this commit.** Call `RegisterLayerActor` only after a genuine GIS-backed actor has been instantiated and provenance independently checked. `bSourceVerified` is a caller assertion; it is not an independent checksum verification. An unregistered layer reports SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE.

Layer categories: terrain, imagery, buildings, roads, parcels, floodplain, sanitary sewer, storm sewer, potable water, electric, gas, telecom, hydraulic results, and proposed construction. Layer visibility is persisted in `Saved/TSM/SceneProfiles/<profile>.json`. The subsystem controls registered actor visibility; it does not yet control Cesium tile selection budgets, weather, camera sequences, LOD, material shaders, or raw GeoPackage ingestion.

## Remaining acceptance gates

1. Verify UE5.8 C++ compilation and plugin dependencies on the authorized Windows runner.
2. Load real Mount Vernon/Point Township GIS features with source hashes, CRS, vertical datum and survey quality metadata.
3. Register the actual scene actors and bind the Slate/UMG menu to `SetLayerVisibility`.
4. Add renderer-side weather and engineering shader controls with observation/simulation/cinematic distinctions.
5. Validate headed city screenshots, streaming FPS/VRAM, packaged Windows 11 offline startup and independent evidence outputs.
